_README: Single source of truth for the ZED depth disparity-offset correction. Read by zed_capture/zed_depth_config.py, which both the capture path and the calibration solvers import. Edit disparity_offset_px here and every consumer follows.
_units: disparity_offset_px is in pixels of disparity at the FULL rectified resolution (2208x1242), i.e. at reference_width_px. baseline_m is metres. Correction: z_true = fx*B / (fx*B/z_reported + offset_px).
_rescaling: A disparity in px is fx*B/z, so it scales EXACTLY as fx does -- and the correction is invariant only when the offset and the fx carry the same scale. A consumer at another resolution must therefore use offset_px * fx_there / reference_fx_px. SCALE BY fx, NOT BY WIDTH: the ZED rectifies separately per resolution, so rectified fx is NOT proportional to width. This camera is 1414.575 at 2208 px but 693.82 at 1280 px, where width-scaling would predict 820.04 -- an 18% error that over-corrects by 14 mm at 1.0 m. corrector_for() does no rescaling at all; it takes whatever offset it is given. The solvers run on native HD2K frames and pass the stored value unchanged; the live ZedSource runs at HD720 and rescales (16.03 * 693.82/1414.575 = 7.86 px).
measured_from: Adopted 2026-08-18 to deploy the zed_calib_fs_001 joint extrinsic (stamped 5.9 px). The offset PHYSICALLY DRIFTED between 2026-08-11 and 2026-08-14 (self-calibration is disabled on this rig, so nothing re-tracks it): the previous 12.0 px was re-derived on 08-14 from the 08-11 zed_calib_003 capture and was stale the day it was written -- it over-corrects post-08-11 captures by ~45 mm at 1 m. Refits on fresh captures agree: zed_calib_007 (08-17) left +6.13 +/- 1.20 px, right +5.68 +/- 1.03 px, both-arm mean +5.90 over 143 frames; zed_calib_fs_001 (08-18) +5.59 +/- 0.95 px. Adopted 5.9 px = the 007 both-arm mean, matching the value stamped in every deployed fs_001 solve. REFIT FROM EVERY NEW CAPTURE before trusting a solve (see _how_to_remeasure); this constant has drifted once already.
_verified: 2026-08-14 (under the then-current 12.0 px): with tag 96.0 mm, the checkerboard-verified intrinsics (factory K exact to ~1%, zero distortion, 75 views at 0.257 px rms) close the loop: the 3-6 % range-scale disagreement between robot-FK and tag/depth ranging on zed_calib_001..003 is fully accounted for by the tag size. 2026-08-18 (5.9 px): the zed_calib_fs_001 joint solve at 5.9 px reaches 3.59 mm mean translation residual over 143 frames (FoundationStereo depth); per-arm FS solves broke the old ~6.7 mm right-arm floor (1.38 mm). Hand-eye residuals: see the re-solve summaries in zsy-testmycode/results/.
_cause: A constant disparity offset, equal to 0.649 deg of relative yaw between the two lenses. SN22456.conf stores CV_2K = 0.0142736 rad = 0.818 deg. Stereolabs self-calibration normally removes this drift at every open(), but on this rig it always FAILS because the black backdrop has no texture. Therefore the drift is never removed.
_ruled_out: fx (AprilTag PnP agrees with robot forward kinematics to 2%), baseline (a wrong baseline scales depth by a constant, but the depth/PnP ratio RISES with distance: 1.114 at 1.09 m to 1.169 at 1.53 m), depth mode (NEURAL/NEURAL_PLUS/ULTRA agree to 0.2%), depth_min, config corruption (byte-identical to the Stereolabs server copy), hardware (ZED_Diagnostic all OK).
WARNING: THIS IS A WORKAROUND FOR A HARDWARE FAULT, NOT A FIX. The value belongs to camera SN22456 in its PRESENT factory calibration. Set disparity_offset_px to 0.0 after you run ZED_Calibration, or after a self-calibration succeeds, or if you swap the camera. If you leave it non-zero after a recalibration it pushes the depth wrong in the OTHER direction. zed_depth_config.check_camera() compares conf_md5 with the file on disk and warns you, but it cannot detect a successful self-calibration, because that does not touch the .conf file.
_how_to_remeasure: Capture a tag dataset across 1.0-1.9 m, then for each frame compute the raw depth at the tag centre and the AprilTag PnP distance, and fit the single offset d that satisfies fx*B/z_depth + d = fx*B/z_pnp. A good fit has a standard deviation under 1 px and no trend against range.
_to_disable_once: Set $ZED_DEPTH_OFFSET_PX=0, or pass --disparity-offset-px 0 to the capture and solver scripts.
